title: Make a family story you can listen to together
task: Turn a relative’s recollection into a short narrated scene they can correct in their own words.
prompt: Use these approved details to draft a two-minute narrated scene. Pause where a name, place or date is missing and ask a follow-up. Mark imaginative illustrations separately and let me approve the script before rendering.
check: Play it to the storyteller. Ask which words sound like theirs and remove details they did not give you permission to share.
inputs: A consenting storyteller, notes and a voice-capable agent
recognition: Gemini Live Agent Challenge · Creative Storyteller winner

title: Find a replacement car part with the right fit
task: Get a shortlist of used parts with fit, shipping and return terms checked before you buy.
prompt: Look for this exact OEM number and revision at the sellers I listed. Separate verified stock from listings that still need a call. Draft the question for each seller and wait for me before contacting anyone.
check: Match the stamped number and connector in the seller’s photo against the old part. Count shipping and the return fee in the comparison.
inputs: Part number, year, trim and a photo
recognition: Gemini Live Agent Challenge · Honorable mention

title: Report a flooded crossing with a usable location
task: Turn a voice note made from a safe place into a road report a maintenance crew can locate.
prompt: Extract the nearest crossing, direction of travel, observation time and what I actually saw. Put a pin on the map and read back the draft. If the location is ambiguous, show the candidates before preparing a report.
check: Check the pin against the named streets and strip faces or plates from attachments. Decide yourself whether to submit.
inputs: A stationary voice note and a map
recognition: Gemini Live Agent Challenge · Honorable mention

title: Rehearse an LED circuit before connecting power
task: Get a second look at the breadboard rows you used for a first electronics project.
prompt: With the board disconnected, compare this photo of my battery-powered LED circuit with the reference diagram. Highlight each wire end and simulate the expected path. Ask for a closer picture if a row number is unreadable.
check: Trace each connection yourself. Confirm the resistor value and polarity against your kit guide before powering it.
inputs: An unpowered beginner circuit, diagram and camera
recognition: Gemini Live Agent Challenge · Honorable mention

title: Navigate a video lesson hands-free
task: Use speech and a pointing gesture to find the diagram, zoom in and replay the demonstration.
prompt: In this lesson, scroll to the diagram I am pointing at, enlarge it, then play the adjacent demonstration. Pause when I say stop. Ask me when two controls are close together.
check: Try it on a public page. Say stop halfway through and confirm you can take back the controls.
inputs: A public lesson and a pointer-aware browser assistant
recognition: Gemini Live Agent Challenge · Multimodal integration and user experience winner

title: Walk through what you learned yesterday
task: Build a small memory palace from your own spoken study notes and revisit one idea at a time.
prompt: Use only this recording of me explaining the chapter. Turn five concepts into objects in themed rooms. When I point at one, ask me to explain it before revealing the passage that inspired it.
check: Visit the rooms in a different order. Correct any object that teaches a connection the recording never made.
inputs: Your own audio notes and a memory-palace agent
recognition: Gemini Live Agent Challenge · Innovation and thought leadership winner

title: Map the trip you actually took
task: Make a map to send friends that distinguishes real walking routes from approximate transit legs.
prompt: Place these stops in the order we visited. Fetch the walking legs, label the train ride as schematic, and give me a phone-friendly map and an image for a postcard. Omit our lodging.
check: Check the two places with similar names and make sure the train leg is visibly different from a measured walking route.
inputs: Stop names in order and how you traveled

title: Trace a family-tree branch back to its documents
task: Build a small family tree where each relationship takes you back to the record that supports it.
prompt: Start with these scans for one deceased relative. Transcribe the names as written, link each relationship to a scan, and list competing dates as separate claims. Give me a private draft tree to review.
check: Pick any parent-child link and follow it back to the record. Leave namesakes separate until a second detail connects them.
inputs: Record copies for one branch of a family

title: Place an unlabeled landscape photo on a map
task: Identify a public landmark by testing skyline and road geometry against multiple candidate viewpoints.
prompt: This is my photo of a public landscape. Compare the skyline, road bend and tower with public maps. Show two candidate viewpoints and the feature that rules one out; leave it unresolved if neither matches.
check: Compare a second angle with a map or landmark photo and record the uncertainty before labeling the archive.
inputs: A landscape photo without people or private addresses

title: Pick the best frame from each photo burst
task: Get a review collection that keeps a sharp expression and makes near-duplicates easy to compare.
prompt: Group the bursts in this album. For each, put a preferred frame and its closest runner-up into a review collection. Give a short reason based on focus, expression or motion. Leave the files and existing ratings alone.
check: View each pair at full size. A technically imperfect frame may be the only one with the expression you want.
inputs: One event album and catalog previews

title: Write audio description into a film’s quiet gaps
task: Create a timed description track that lets a listener follow the action between lines of dialogue.
prompt: Locate the quiet intervals in this short film. Draft only the visual details a listener needs next, synthesize a scratch track and flag cues that cannot fit at a comfortable pace.
check: Listen once with the screen off. Check that descriptions finish before speech resumes and that the key visual reveal makes sense.
inputs: A video you can share, its dialogue and an audio editor
sourceLabel: Microsoft Seeing AI team · audio description workflow

title: Keep a picture-book character recognizable across chapters
task: Give an illustrator a proof sheet that reveals changes in a character’s face, clothing and scale.
prompt: Take this approved character sheet and three manuscript scenes. Make small proofs for each scene, line them up, mark continuity errors, and revise only the failed panels. Leave space for the typesetter.
check: Check the same identifying details in each proof and view the approved art at its intended print size.
inputs: An approved character sheet and three scene descriptions

title: Hear whether a mix correction actually helped
task: Compare the same section of a song before and after one proposed mix change.
prompt: In a copy of this REAPER session, measure the loud chorus, identify one track masking the vocal, and propose a single change. Export matched-level before and after clips with the same start and end.
check: Listen blind at matched loudness. Keep the change only if the words are clearer without losing the instrument you like.
inputs: A multitrack session and a REAPER-connected agent
sourceLabel: REAPER Daemon · measurement and editing guide

title: Block out a game level before making the art
task: Get an editable 3D scene that tests whether the player can read the path and spot the goal.
prompt: Build a low-detail dungeon with one entrance, a bend and a guarded exit. Put the camera at player height and render three points along the route. Revise the geometry where the goal disappears too early.
check: Walk the scene yourself and inspect the three camera frames. Decide what to move before spending time on textures.
inputs: A level sketch, Blender and an agent with scene access

title: Proof a slide deck in both the browser and PDF
task: Deliver the same presentation in two formats without losing a chart label or clipping a footnote.
prompt: Build a short deck from this approved copy and style sample. Export a PDF, inspect every slide for overflow at presentation size, and return thumbnails of the browser and PDF versions side by side.
check: Read the smallest chart label on the exported slide. Check each figure against the supplied copy and open the deck on another screen.
inputs: Approved copy, figures and a brand reference
sourceLabel: Slides Agent · example deck and export checks

title: Find which blocks a proposed service area misses
task: Overlay a distance buffer and a neighborhood map to show where coverage ends.
prompt: Using copies of these QGIS layers, draw a 500-metre buffer around each site and mark blocks it misses. Produce a map with a scale, unit and legend; keep the original layers intact.
check: Measure one boundary by hand in a projected coordinate system. Label the buffer as straight-line distance, since a river can make a short walk impossible.
inputs: Site points, block boundaries and QGIS
sourceLabel: QGent · QGIS buffers, overlays and map export

title: Audition an immersive chorus before rendering the song
task: Compare a short spatial mix with the original and decide whether a full render is worth it.
prompt: Use only this rights-cleared chorus excerpt. I approve sending the excerpt to Spatial9 for a private preview. Return the spatial version alongside the same passage from the original. Ask before sending a full track, spending credits or publishing anything.
check: Switch between the two excerpts on the headphones your audience uses. Check that the lead stays intelligible.
inputs: A song you own, chorus timestamps and a render service

title: Cut a clip that keeps the speaker’s qualification
task: Produce a vertical excerpt that retains the sentence explaining when a claim holds.
prompt: Find a self-contained answer in this interview I own. Give me two timestamped options, include the speaker’s qualification, then make a private rough cut of my choice. Keep their face and any referenced object in frame.
check: Watch the minute before and after the clip. Reject the edit if it changes who or what the answer was about.
inputs: Your interview recording and permission to edit it
sourceLabel: n8n directory · Gemini and FFmpeg clip workflow

title: Catch a duplicate invoice before it reaches approval
task: Turn an invoice batch into a review queue with duplicates and arithmetic errors called out.
prompt: Read these sample invoices into a temporary sheet. Match supplier, invoice number and total, then compare line sums with the amount due. Link every suspect row to its PDF and wait for review.
check: Include a known duplicate and a legitimate second invoice from the same supplier. Verify that only the duplicate is held.
inputs: Sample invoice PDFs and a scratch spreadsheet
sourceLabel: n8n directory · invoice validation and approval

title: Find the internal mentor behind a development goal
task: Convert one piece of feedback into a practice assignment with a relevant person and reading attached.
prompt: Use the skill list and opt-in mentor directory to turn this piece of feedback into one task I can practice this month. Cite the internal guide and show why the suggested mentor is relevant. Draft the introduction for me to send.
check: Check the guide is accessible to me and the mentor opted into this topic. Agree with my manager on what improvement looks like.
inputs: One development goal, an internal learning list and mentor directory
sourceLabel: Microsoft Agent Academy · first-place recruit project
recognition: Agent Academy · first place, Recruit track

title: Check a vendor contract against your own rulebook
task: Give a procurement reviewer a clause-by-clause exception list with page references.
prompt: Take the vendor’s draft and the approved procurement checklist. For each rule, quote the relevant clause and page or mark it missing. Flag exceptions for our reviewer and leave signature and approval untouched.
check: Look up the cited clause for every exception and check a known pass. Have the contract owner decide what needs negotiation.
inputs: A draft contract and an approved procurement checklist
sourceLabel: Microsoft Agent Academy · VendorGuard winning entry
recognition: Agent Academy · first place, Operative track
